newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek blue chips trade firmer, seen bullish.
newsitem.headline: Greek blue chips trade firmer, seen bullish.

text.p: The Athens general share index was trading 0.45 percent higher on Wednesday and market watchers anticipated a bullish session led by a rise in blue chips.

"The market looks certainly bullish in the short-run. Blue chips seem to be the leaders of the rise and we expect their upward trend to continue," said investment manager George Kartalis, at Alico Eurobank Mutual Funds.

Market movements are milder now. Instead of seeing the benchmark index gain or lose up to 6.0 or 7.0 percent in one day, as it did in late February, its recent fluctuations have ranged between 0.2-2.0 percent, he added.

"The market's latest rise has been triggered by Greek retail investors, who were scared away from the bourse when the market lost 7.0 percent in one session. Now they are staying in the market, because this new milder rise makes them feel more confident," he said.
Foreign investors are still interested in Greek equities but we no longer have massive buys, because they are waiting to see where the market will go in the short-term, he added.
"But I am definetely optimistic this time and I think this bull market will last," said Kartalis.
The Athens general share index was trading 0.45 percent or 6.49 points higher at 1,443.04 from Tuesday's 1,436.55 close, after opening at 1,436.61.

The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted higher at 1,061.0-1,099.0. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, were up 80 drachmas at 6,560 a new high.

The recently launched ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $59.12-$60.82. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The recently issued ING Baring Financial Products American- style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted higher at 2,387-2,586 drachmas.
The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
